root_cause.mechanism: When importing or inspecting __main__ (or modules where __spec__ is None), calling importlib.util.find_spec raises a ValueError (__main__.__spec__ is None). Recent changes in Flask replaced pkgutil.get_loader with importlib.util.find_spec without wrapping all find_spec calls in try...except (ImportError, ValueError). Wrapping find_spec calls in try...except (ImportError, ValueError) correctly handles missing specs/ValueError and falls back to loading/cwd logic.

hypotheses.text: importlib.util.find_spec("__main__") raises ValueError: __main__.__spec__ is None when __main__ has no __spec__ (e.g. running python -c or direct script execution in some python versions/setups where __spec__ is None), but find_spec expects a valid module name or raises ValueError for __main__ if spec is None.
hypotheses.predicts: Running a python script that instantiates Flask(__name__) when __name__ == '__main__' will succeed if we handle or check for __main__.__spec__ being None or pass when root_mod_name == "__main__" before calling importlib.util.find_spec(__main__)

hypotheses.predicts: Wrapping importlib.util.find_spec in try...except (ImportError, ValueError) correctly catches ValueError when __main__.__spec__ is None or module name is invalid, falling back to the loader/cwd path logic.
hypotheses.evidence: Line 821 has try...except (ImportError, ValueError), but line 858 does not have try...except (ImportError, ValueError). When line 821 hits ValueError, it falls through to line 858 which calls importlib.util.find_spec(root_mod_name) without try...except, raising ValueError: __main__.__spec__ is None.
